edges.description: A heterozygous missense Kcnn2 allele that reduces SK2 channel activity.

nodes.description: SK channels carry part of the afterhyperpolarization that follows action potentials and so set neuronal firing patterns. In the frissonnant Kcnn2 mouse, central vestibular neurons show lasting changes in afterhyperpolarization and firing. Neuronal firing has not been studied in patient-derived cells.

evidence.reference_title: Behavioral effects of a deletion in Kcnn2, the gene encoding the SK2 subunit of small-conductance Ca2+-activated K+ channels.
evidence.snippet: Intracellular electrophysiological recordings of central vestibular neurons revealed permanent alterations of the AHP and firing behavior that might cause the tremor and associated locomotor deficits.

evidence.reference_title: Behavioral effects of a deletion in Kcnn2, the gene encoding the SK2 subunit of small-conductance Ca2+-activated K+ channels.
evidence.snippet: Small-conductance Ca(2+)-activated potassium (SK) channels are heteromeric complexes of SK alpha-subunits and calmodulin that modulate membrane excitability, are responsible for part of the after-hyperpolarization (AHP) following action potentials, and thus control the firing patterns and excitability of most central neurons.

evidence.reference_title: K(Ca) 2.2 (KCNN2): A physiologically and therapeutically important potassium channel.
evidence.snippet: KCa 2.x channels inhibit excitatory postsynaptic potentials (EPSPs) in neuronal dendrites and contribute to the medium afterhyperpolarization (mAHP) that follows the action potential bursts.

evidence.reference_title: Variants in the SK2 channel gene (KCNN2) lead to dominant neurodevelopmental movement disorders.
evidence.snippet: Patients with KCNN2 variants had motor and language developmental delay, intellectual disability often associated with early-onset movement disorders comprising cerebellar ataxia and/or extrapyramidal symptoms.

evidence.reference_title: Early-Onset Neurodevelopmental Movement Disorder Secondary to Novel Mutation in KCNN2.
evidence.snippet: Developmental delay occurred in 90% of individuals, and movement disorders in 60% (tremor, ataxia, myoclonus, dystonia, chorea, tics).

nodes.description: Heterozygous KCNN2 variants (frameshift, nonsense, splice site, in-frame deletion and missense) reduce SK2 channel activity. Five of six variants tested by patch clamp in the founding series caused loss of function. In HEK293 cells, channels carrying pathogenic missense changes give no measurable current, and pore-lining mutants also suppress co-expressed wild-type SK2, so a dominant-negative effect may add to haploinsufficiency for some missense alleles. In a C. elegans knock-in study most disease variants behaved as loss of function, but I359M behaved as gain of function, so the direction of effect is not settled for every allele.

evidence.snippet: All variants tested but one, which was reclassified to uncertain significance, led to a loss-of-function of SK2 channels.

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function K(Ca)2.2 mutations abolish channel activity.
evidence.snippet: No measurable current was detected from HEK293 cells heterologously expressing these pathogenic KCa2.2 mutants.

evidence.reference_title: K(Ca) 2.2 (KCNN2): A physiologically and therapeutically important potassium channel.
evidence.snippet: Studies have revealed that autosomal dominant neurodevelopmental movement disorders resembling rodent symptoms are caused by heterozygous loss-of-function mutations, which are most likely to induce KCNN2 haploinsufficiency.

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function K(Ca)2.2 mutations abolish channel activity.
evidence.snippet: When coexpressed with the KCa2.2_WT channel, mutations of the pore-lining amino acid residues (I360M, Y362C, G363S, and I389V) and two proline substitutions (L174P and L433P) dominant negatively suppressed and completely abolished the activity of the coexpressed KCa2.2_WT channel.

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function K(Ca)2.2 mutations abolish channel activity.
evidence.snippet: Coexpression of the KCa2.2_I289N and the KCa2.2_WT channels reduced the apparent Ca2+ sensitivity compared with the KCa2.2_WT channel, which was rescued by a KCa2.2 positive modulator.

evidence.reference_title: Functional validation of human SK channels variants causing NEDMAB and Zimmermann-Laband syndrome-3 in C. elegans.
evidence.snippet: NEDMAB mutations exhibited more complex phenotypic effects. Most caused a loss-of-function phenotype, indistinguishable from null mutants, while one displayed a clear gain-of-function effect.

evidence.reference_title: Functional validation of human SK channels variants causing NEDMAB and Zimmermann-Laband syndrome-3 in C. elegans.
evidence.snippet: Strikingly, the I359M NEDMAB mutation caused gain-of-function and not loss-of-function effects.
